'''Lauren Kiyomi Williams''' (born {{abbr|c.|circa}} 1978) is an American mathematician known for her work on [[cluster algebra]]s, [[tropical geometry]], [[algebraic combinatorics]], [[Amplituhedron|amplituhedra]], and the positive [[Grassmannian]].<ref name=quanta/> She is Dwight Parker Robinson Professor of Mathematics at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="cv">{{citation|title=Lauren K. Williams|url=http://www.math.harvard.edu/~williams/|accessdate=September 23, 2018}}.</ref>
She was awarded a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Fellowship]] in 2025.<ref name="towfighi">{{citation |last=Towfighi |first=Michaela |title=MacArthur Foundation Announces 2025 'Genius Grant' Winners | newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 8, 2025 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/08/arts/design/macarthur-foundation-2025-genius-grant-winners.html}}</ref>

==Education==
Williams's father is an engineer; her mother is third-generation [[Japanese Americans|Japanese American]]. She grew up in Los Angeles, where she was born. Her interest in mathematics was sparked by winning a fourth-grade mathematics contest.<ref name=quanta>{{citation|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-mathematicians-adventure-through-the-physical-world-20201216/|title=A Mathematician's Unanticipated Journey Through the Physical World|magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]]|first=Kevin|last=Hartnett|date=December 16, 2020}}</ref> She graduated as [[valedictorian]] of [[Palos Verdes Peninsula High School]] in 1996.<ref name="cv"/> As a high school student, Williams attended the 1994 [[Research Science Institute]] at [[MIT]],<ref name=rsi>{{citation|url=https://www.cee.org/about-us/1994-rickoids|title=RSI 1994|accessdate=October 9, 2025}}</ref> where she conducted research with Satomi Okazaki, a student of her eventual Ph.D. advisor [[Richard P. Stanley]].<ref name=quanta/> She graduated [[magna cum laude]] from [[Harvard University]] in 2000 with an A.B. in mathematics<ref name="cv"/> and in 2001 completed Part III of the [[Mathematical Tripos]] with distinction at Cambridge University in England. In 2005 she received her Ph.D. from [[MIT]] under the supervision of Stanley.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=92849}}</ref> Her dissertation was titled ''Combinatorial aspects of total positivity''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/31163|title=Combinatorial aspects of total positivity|first=Lauren Kiyomi|last=Williams|date=October 12, 2005|via=dspace.mit.edu}}</ref>

==Work==
After postdoctoral positions at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and Harvard, Williams rejoined the Berkeley mathematics department as an assistant professor in 2009, and was promoted to associate professor in 2013 and then full professor in 2016.<ref name="cv"/>

Starting in the fall of 2018, she rejoined the Harvard mathematics department as a full professor, making her the second ever tenured female math professor at Harvard. The first, [[Sophie Morel]], left Harvard in 2012.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2018/4/6/aurox-williams-hired-math/|title=Math Dept Hires 2nd-Ever Female Tenured Prof, Ending Six-Year Drought |website= The Harvard Crimson|language=en|access-date=May 1, 2018}}</ref>

Along with colleagues Olya Mandelshtam (her former student, now an assistant professor at the [[University of Waterloo]]) and [[Sylvie Corteel]], in 2018 Williams developed a new characterization of both symmetric and nonsymmetric [[Macdonald polynomials]] using the combinatorial exclusion process.<ref name=exclusion>{{cite arXiv |first1=Sylvie|last1=Corteel |first2=Olya|last2=Mandelshtam |first3=Lauren|last3=Williams |eprint=1811.01024 |title=From multiline queues to Macdonald polynomials via the exclusion process |year=2018 |class=math.CO |mode=cs2}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2012, she became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|accessdate=May 31, 2016}}.</ref> She is the 2016 winner of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] and [[Microsoft]] [[AWM–Microsoft Research Prize in Algebra and Number Theory|Research Prize in Algebra and Number Theory]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B3jjMnRu5mxWVXFkRnp5SnMyWjc5M3hrYWtKdG0tZFAxWThv/view|title=Lauren Williams wins the second AWM-Microsoft Research Prize in Algebra and Number Theory|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|date=June 3, 2015|accessdate=May 31, 2016}}.</ref> In 2022 she was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Durrick |first=Mallory |title=Announcements |url=https://www.gf.org/announcements/ |access-date=July 4, 2022 |website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2025 she was awarded a [[MacArthur Fellows Program|MacArthur Fellowship]].<ref name="towfighi"/>
